title: Indian History (Ancient, Medieval, Modern & North-East)
why: History gives 3–5 GK questions a year, and they are almost always one-line 'who/where/which book' facts — 2022 asked about Sir Syed Ahmad Khan's Anglo-Muhammadan Oriental College and 'Gokhale, My Political Guru'. The modern period (INC sessions, Gandhian movements, reformers, books) is the richest seam, and a North-East exam can add Ahom and Anglo-Burmese questions. Learn the tables; the questions test recall, not interpretation.

lessons.title: Ancient India I: Indus Valley, Vedic Age, Buddhism & Jainism
lessons.body:
### Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilisation — c. 2600–1900 BCE (mature phase)

- Bronze Age, urban; first discovered at **Harappa (1921, Daya Ram Sahni)** on the Ravi, then **Mohenjo-daro (1922, R.D. Banerji)** on the Indus; ASI DG **Sir John Marshall** announced it (1924).
- Features: grid-plan towns, burnt bricks, covered drains, citadel + lower town, standard weights, seals (steatite; unicorn motif), **undeciphered script** (boustrophedon), cotton earliest known, no iron, no horse (debated), no temples found.

| Site | River / State (country) | Famous for |
|---|---|---|
| **Harappa** | Ravi — Punjab (Pak) | Granaries, first site excavated |
| **Mohenjo-daro** | Indus — Sindh (Pak) | **Great Bath**, Great Granary, bronze **Dancing Girl**, bearded **Priest-King**, Pashupati seal |
| **Lothal** | Bhogava — Gujarat | **Dockyard**, bead factory, rice husk |
| **Kalibangan** | Ghaggar — Rajasthan | **Ploughed field**, fire altars, "black bangles" |
| **Dholavira** | Rann of Kutch — Gujarat | Water reservoirs, **signboard**; UNESCO World Heritage (2021) |
| **Rakhigarhi** | Haryana | Largest Harappan site in India |
| Chanhudaro | Sindh (Pak) | Bead-making; the only city **without a citadel** |
| Banawali | Haryana | Toy plough |
| Ropar | Punjab (India) | Dog buried with man |
| Surkotada | Gujarat | Horse remains |

### Vedic Age (c. 1500–600 BCE)

| Early Vedic (Rigvedic) | Later Vedic |
|---|---|
| Sapta Sindhu region; pastoral; cattle = wealth | Ganga–Yamuna doab; agriculture; **iron** (*krishna ayas*); Painted Grey Ware |
| Tribal assemblies **Sabha, Samiti**, Vidatha; women attended | Kingship grew; varna rigid; Sabha/Samiti declined |
| Gods: Indra (most hymns), Agni, Varuna, Soma | Prajapati, Vishnu, Rudra rose |
| **Battle of Ten Kings** (Dasarajna) on the **Parushni (Ravi)** — Sudas of the Bharatas won | Mahajanapadas emerge |

| Text | Remember |
|---|---|
| **Rigveda** | Oldest; 10 mandalas, 1,028 hymns; **Gayatri Mantra** (Mandala III, to Savitri); Purusha Sukta (Mandala X, varna) |
| Samaveda | Chants/melodies — origin of Indian music |
| Yajurveda | Sacrificial formulas (prose + verse) |
| Atharvaveda | Charms, spells, folk medicine |
| Upanishads (Vedanta) | Philosophy; **"Satyameva Jayate" — Mundaka Upanishad** |
| Epics | Ramayana (Valmiki), Mahabharata (Ved Vyasa; Bhagavad Gita is part of Bhishma Parva) |

### Buddhism & Jainism (6th century BCE)

| | **Gautama Buddha** | **Vardhamana Mahavira** |
|---|---|---|
| Birth | **Lumbini** (Nepal), Shakya clan | **Kundagrama** near Vaishali, Jnatrika clan |
| Key event | Enlightenment at **Bodh Gaya** under the pipal tree | Kaivalya on the bank of Rijupalika |
| First sermon | **Sarnath** (Deer Park) — *Dharmachakra Pravartana*; UNESCO World Heritage Site (2026) | — |
| Death | **Kushinagar** (Mahaparinirvana) | **Pavapuri** |
| Teaching | Four Noble Truths, Eightfold Path, Middle Way | Five vows incl. ahimsa; 24th Tirthankara (1st Rishabhanatha, 23rd Parshvanatha) |
| Sects | Hinayana / Mahayana (split at 4th Council) | Shvetambara / Digambara |

| Buddhist Council | Place | Patron | Chair |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1st | Rajagriha | Ajatashatru | Mahakassapa |
| 2nd | Vaishali | Kalashoka | Sabakami |
| 3rd | Pataliputra | **Ashoka** | Moggaliputta Tissa |
| 4th | Kashmir (Kundalavana) | **Kanishka** | Vasumitra (Ashvaghosha vice) |

- **16 Mahajanapadas** (Anguttara Nikaya); **Magadha** rose under Haryanka (Bimbisara, Ajatashatru) → Shishunaga → Nanda (Mahapadma Nanda). Capitals: Rajagriha then **Pataliputra**.
- **Alexander** invaded 326 BCE; **Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum)** against **Porus**.

lessons.title: Ancient India II: Mauryas, Post-Mauryans, Guptas, Harsha & the South
lessons.body:
### Mauryan Empire (c. 322–185 BCE)

| Ruler | Facts |
|---|---|
| **Chandragupta Maurya** | Overthrew Nandas with **Chanakya/Kautilya** (*Arthashastra*); defeated **Seleucus Nicator** (305 BCE); **Megasthenes** (Seleucus's envoy) wrote ***Indica***; became Jain, died at Shravanabelagola |
| Bindusara | "Amitraghata"; Ajivika sympathies |
| **Ashoka** | **Kalinga War (261 BCE)** → Dhamma; edicts mostly in **Prakrit, Brahmi script** (Kharosthi in NW, Greek & Aramaic in Afghanistan); first deciphered by **James Prinsep (1837)**; called himself *Devanampiya Piyadasi*; sent Mahendra & Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka |
| End | Last ruler **Brihadratha** killed by **Pushyamitra Shunga** (c. 185 BCE) |

- **National Emblem** = Lion Capital of Ashoka at **Sarnath**; motto "Satyameva Jayate" below it. Ashoka Chakra (24 spokes) on the flag.

### Post-Mauryan (c. 200 BCE–300 CE)

| Dynasty | Remember |
|---|---|
| Shunga, Kanva | Brahmanical revival; Patanjali (Mahabhashya) |
| Indo-Greeks | **Menander (Milinda)** — dialogue with Nagasena in *Milindapanho*; first coins attributable to named kings, and generally credited with the first gold coins in India (Kushanas — Vima Kadphises — first issued gold coins on a large scale) |
| **Kushanas** | **Kanishka** — **Saka era (78 CE)** (India's national calendar), 4th Buddhist Council, **Gandhara** (Greco-Roman) & **Mathura** schools of art; court: Ashvaghosha (*Buddhacharita*), Nagarjuna, **Charaka** (medicine) |
| Satavahanas | Deccan; Gautamiputra Satakarni; lead/potin coins; Nasik inscription |
| **Sangam Age** (Tamil) | Cheras, Cholas, Pandyas; *Tolkappiyam* (grammar), ***Tirukkural*** (**Thiruvalluvar**), ***Silappatikaram*** (Ilango Adigal), *Manimekalai* (Sittalai Sattanar) |

### Gupta Age (c. 320–550 CE) — "Classical / Golden Age"

| Ruler | Facts |
|---|---|
| Sri Gupta | Founder |
| **Chandragupta I** | Started **Gupta era (320 CE)**; married Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi |
| **Samudragupta** | **Allahabad Pillar (Prayag Prashasti)** by court poet **Harisena**; "**Napoleon of India**" (V.A. Smith); veena-playing coins |
| **Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya)** | Defeated Shakas; **Fa-Hien** visited; Navaratnas incl. **Kalidasa**; Mehrauli iron pillar (rust-free) |
| Kumaragupta I | Founded **Nalanda** university |
| Skandagupta | Repelled the **Hunas** |

| Scholar | Work |
|---|---|
| **Aryabhata** | *Aryabhatiya* — place value, π ≈ 3.1416, Earth rotates; India's first satellite named after him (1975) |
| Varahamihira | *Brihat Samhita*, *Pancha Siddhantika* |
| Brahmagupta | *Brahmasphutasiddhanta* (rules for zero) |
| **Kalidasa** | *Abhijnanashakuntalam*, *Meghaduta*, *Raghuvamsha*, *Kumarasambhava* |
| Vishakhadatta | *Mudrarakshasa*; Shudraka — *Mrichchhakatika*; Amarasimha — *Amarakosha* |

- Art: **Ajanta** paintings (Buddhist; many under Vakatakas), Dashavatara temple **Deogarh**, Sarnath Buddha.

### Harsha & the South

| Dynasty / ruler | Remember |
|---|---|
| **Harshavardhana** (606–647) | Capital **Kannauj**; **Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang)** — *Si-yu-ki*; **Banabhatta** — *Harshacharita*, *Kadambari*; Harsha wrote *Ratnavali, Nagananda, Priyadarshika*; defeated by **Pulakeshin II** (Chalukya) on the **Narmada** |
| Chalukyas of Badami | **Aihole inscription** (Ravikirti) records Pulakeshin II's victory |
| **Pallavas** (Kanchi) | **Mahabalipuram** rathas & Shore Temple (Narasimhavarman I "Mamalla", Rajasimha) |
| **Rashtrakutas** | **Kailasa temple, Ellora** (monolithic) — **Krishna I**; Amoghavarsha — *Kavirajamarga* |
| **Cholas** | **Rajaraja I** — Brihadeeswara temple, Thanjavur; **Rajendra I** — Gangaikonda Cholapuram, naval raid on **Srivijaya**; village self-government (Uttaramerur inscription) |
| Kamarupa (Assam) | **Bhaskaravarman** — ally of Harsha, host to Hiuen Tsang |

lessons.title: Medieval India I: Delhi Sultanate, Vijayanagara & Bhakti-Sufi
lessons.body:
### Early Turkish invasions
| Year | Event |
|---|---|
| 712 | **Muhammad bin Qasim** conquers Sindh (Arabs) |
| 1000–1027 | **Mahmud of Ghazni** — 17 raids; **Somnath (1025)**; **Al-Biruni** — *Kitab-ul-Hind* |
| 1191 | **First Battle of Tarain** — Prithviraj Chauhan defeats **Muhammad Ghori** |
| 1192 | **Second Battle of Tarain** — Ghori defeats Prithviraj |
| 1194 | Battle of Chandawar — Ghori defeats Jaichand (Gahadavala) |

### Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526) — "Slave, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi" (SKTSL)

| Dynasty | Ruler — key facts |
|---|---|
| **Slave/Mamluk** (1206–90) | **Qutbuddin Aibak** — began **Qutub Minar**, Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, "Lakh Bakhsh"; **Iltutmish** — completed Qutub Minar, silver **tanka** & copper **jital**, *iqta* system, **Turkan-i-Chahalgani** (the Forty); **Razia Sultan** — first & only woman ruler of Delhi; **Balban** — theory of kingship, *sijda* & *paibos*, "blood and iron" |
| **Khalji** (1290–1320) | **Alauddin Khalji** — **market control**, standing army paid in cash, *dagh* (branding horses) & *chehra* (descriptive roll), repelled Mongols, **Alai Darwaza**, Siri Fort; general **Malik Kafur**; poet **Amir Khusrau** ("Tuti-e-Hind") |
| **Tughlaq** (1320–1414) | **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** — capital to **Daulatabad (1327)**, **token currency** (bronze/copper), Moroccan traveller **Ibn Battuta** (*Rihla*) served as qazi; **Firoz Shah** — canals, *jizya* on Brahmins, moved Ashokan pillars to Delhi; **Timur's invasion 1398** |
| Sayyid (1414–51) | Khizr Khan |
| **Lodi** (1451–1526) | Bahlul; **Sikandar Lodi** founded **Agra (1504)**, *Gaz-i-Sikandari*; **Ibrahim Lodi** killed at **First Panipat (1526)** |

### Deccan kingdoms
| Kingdom | Facts |
|---|---|
| **Vijayanagara** (1336) | Founded by **Harihara & Bukka** (Sangama dynasty) on the Tungabhadra (Hampi); **Krishnadevaraya** (Tuluva) — *Amuktamalyada* (Telugu), *Ashtadiggajas*; visitors Nicolo Conti, Abdur Razzaq, Domingo Paes; destroyed at **Battle of Talikota / Rakshasi-Tangadi (1565)** by Deccan sultanates |
| **Bahmani** (1347) | **Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah**; minister **Mahmud Gawan** (madrasa at Bidar); split into 5 sultanates (Bijapur — Gol Gumbaz; Golconda — Qutb Shahi) |

### Bhakti & Sufi
| Saint | Region / contribution |
|---|---|
| Ramanuja, Madhva, Nimbarka | South Indian Vaishnava philosophers |
| **Kabir** | Weaver-poet, *dohas*, against idolatry & caste; *Bijak* |
| **Guru Nanak** (1469, Talwandi) | Founder of Sikhism; *langar*; Kartarpur |
| Chaitanya Mahaprabhu | Bengal; *kirtan*, Krishna bhakti |
| Mirabai, Surdas, **Tulsidas** (*Ramcharitmanas*, under Akbar) | Rajasthan / Braj / Awadhi |
| **Srimanta Sankardeva** | Assam; **Ekasarana Dharma**, **Sattras & Namghars**, *Borgeet*, *Ankiya Naat*, Sattriya dance |
| Namdev, Tukaram, Eknath, **Jnaneshwar** (*Jnaneshwari*) | Maharashtra |
| **Moinuddin Chishti** | Ajmer — Chishti order in India |
| **Nizamuddin Auliya** | Delhi — disciple Amir Khusrau |

lessons.title: Medieval India II: Mughals, Marathas & Sikh Gurus
lessons.body:
### The Mughals (1526–1857)

| Emperor | Key facts |
|---|---|
| **Babur** (1526–30) | **1st Panipat 1526** (Ibrahim Lodi; first use of field artillery/*tulughma*); **Khanwa 1527** (Rana Sanga); Chanderi 1528 (Medini Rai); Ghaghra 1529 (Afghans); memoir ***Baburnama*** in Turki |
| **Humayun** | Lost to **Sher Shah** at **Chausa (1539)** & **Kannauj/Bilgram (1540)**; regained 1555; died falling from library stairs (Sher Mandal, 1556); *Humayun-nama* by sister **Gulbadan Begum** |
| **Sher Shah Suri** (1540–45) | Silver **rupiya**, **Grand Trunk Road** (Sadak-e-Azam) repaired/extended, sarais, *patta & qabuliyat*; tomb at **Sasaram** |
| **Akbar** (1556–1605) | **2nd Panipat 1556** (Hemu; regent Bairam Khan); **Haldighati 1576** (Maharana Pratap vs Man Singh); abolished pilgrim tax (1563) & **jizya (1564)**; **Mansabdari**; **Ibadat Khana (1575)** at Fatehpur Sikri; **Din-i-Ilahi (1582)**; **Buland Darwaza** (Gujarat victory); **Todar Mal's Zabti / Dahsala** revenue; Navaratnas — Birbal, Tansen, **Abul Fazl** (*Akbarnama*, *Ain-i-Akbari*), Faizi, Todar Mal, Man Singh, Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan |
| **Jahangir** (1605–27) | "Chain of justice"; Nur Jahan; **Sir Thomas Roe (1615)** secured English trade at Surat; executed Guru Arjan Dev (1606); *Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri* |
| **Shah Jahan** (1628–58) | "Golden age of architecture" — **Taj Mahal** (for Mumtaz Mahal), **Red Fort** & **Jama Masjid** Delhi, **Peacock Throne**, Shahjahanabad |
| **Aurangzeb** (1658–1707) | Reimposed **jizya (1679)**; executed **Guru Tegh Bahadur (1675)**; long Deccan wars; died 1707 at Ahmednagar; Bibi-ka-Maqbara (Aurangabad) built by his son Azam Shah |
| Later | **Nadir Shah (1739)** — took Peacock Throne & Kohinoor; **3rd Panipat (1761)** — **Ahmad Shah Abdali** beat the Marathas; **Bahadur Shah Zafar** — last emperor, exiled to Rangoon after 1857 |

### Marathas
- **Shivaji** (b. 1630, Shivneri) — crowned **1674 at Raigad**; *Ashtapradhan* council; *chauth* (1/4) & *sardeshmukhi* (1/10); guerrilla warfare; Treaty of Purandar (1665) with Jai Singh.
- **Peshwas**: Balaji Vishwanath, **Baji Rao I** (expansion north), Balaji Baji Rao (Nana Saheb; 3rd Panipat).

### Sikh Gurus
| Guru | Remember |
|---|---|
| 1 Nanak | Founder |
| 2 Angad | **Gurmukhi** script |
| 3 Amar Das | Manji system; against sati & purdah |
| 4 Ram Das | Founded **Amritsar** |
| 5 **Arjan Dev** | Compiled **Adi Granth (1604)**; Harmandir Sahib; executed by Jahangir (1606) |
| 6 Hargobind | **Akal Takht**; militarised the Sikhs |
| 9 **Tegh Bahadur** | Executed by Aurangzeb (1675) |
| 10 **Gobind Singh** | Founded **Khalsa (1699)** at Anandpur Sahib; declared Guru Granth Sahib the eternal Guru |
- **Maharaja Ranjit Singh** — Sikh kingdom at Lahore (1799); Treaty of Amritsar 1809 with the British.

lessons.title: Europeans, British Expansion, Governors-General & the Revolt of 1857
lessons.body:
### Coming of the Europeans
| Power | Key date / place |
|---|---|
| **Portuguese** | **Vasco da Gama** at **Calicut, 1498** (ruler Zamorin); **Albuquerque** took **Goa (1510)** |
| Dutch | VOC 1602; Masulipatnam, Pulicat; defeated by Travancore at Colachel (1741) |
| **English** | East India Company charter by **Elizabeth I, 31 Dec 1600**; first factory Masulipatnam (1611); first permanent factory **Surat (1613)** |
| Danes | 1616; Tranquebar, Serampore |
| **French** | 1664 (Colbert); Pondicherry HQ; **Dupleix**; lost at **Wandiwash (1760)** |

### British expansion — battles & wars
| Event | Year | Parties / result |
|---|---|---|
| **Battle of Plassey** | **23 June 1757** | **Robert Clive** beat **Siraj-ud-Daulah** (Mir Jafar's treachery) |
| Battle of Wandiwash | 1760 | English (Eyre Coote) beat French — 3rd Carnatic War |
| Third Battle of Panipat | 1761 | Abdali beat Marathas |
| **Battle of Buxar** | **1764** | English (Hector Munro) beat **Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah & Shah Alam II** |
| Treaty of Allahabad | 1765 | Company got **Diwani** of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa → dual government |
| Anglo-Mysore Wars | 1767–99 | **Tipu Sultan** killed at Srirangapatna (1799) |
| Anglo-Maratha Wars | 1775–1818 | Peshwa-ship abolished (1818) |
| Anglo-Sikh Wars | 1845–49 | Punjab annexed (1849) |

### Governors-General & Viceroys — the one-liners
| Name | Remember for |
|---|---|
| **Warren Hastings** | First Governor-General of Bengal (**Regulating Act 1773**); Asiatic Society (1784, by William Jones) |
| **Cornwallis** | **Permanent Settlement (1793)**; civil services; Cornwallis Code |
| **Wellesley** | **Subsidiary Alliance (1798)** — first accepted by Hyderabad |
| **William Bentinck** | First **GG of India** (Charter Act 1833); **abolished Sati (1829)**; English education (Macaulay's Minute, 1835); suppressed thugs |
| **Dalhousie** | **Doctrine of Lapse** (Satara first, Jhansi, Nagpur); annexed Awadh (1856, misgovernment); **first railway Bombay–Thane (16 Apr 1853)**; telegraph; Wood's Despatch (1854) |
| **Canning** | 1857 revolt; **last GG & first Viceroy** (1858); Widow Remarriage Act 1856; universities of Calcutta, Bombay, Madras (1857) |
| Mayo | First census (1872, non-synchronous); assassinated in the Andamans |
| Lytton | Vernacular Press Act (1878); Delhi Durbar 1877 |
| **Ripon** | **Local self-government (1882)** — "father of local self-government"; first factory act (1881); **Ilbert Bill** (1883); first synchronous census (1881) |
| Dufferin | INC founded (1885) |
| **Curzon** | **Partition of Bengal (1905)**; Ancient Monuments Preservation Act (1904) |
| Minto II | **Morley–Minto reforms (1909)** — separate electorates for Muslims |
| **Hardinge II** | **Capital moved Calcutta → Delhi (1911)**; Bengal partition annulled |
| Chelmsford | Montagu–Chelmsford reforms (1919, dyarchy); Rowlatt Act; **Jallianwala Bagh (13 Apr 1919)** |
| Irwin | Simon Commission; Dandi March; Gandhi–Irwin Pact (1931) |
| Willingdon | Communal Award & Poona Pact (1932) |
| Linlithgow | Longest-serving; August Offer (1940); Cripps; Quit India |
| Wavell | Shimla Conference (1945); Cabinet Mission |
| **Mountbatten** | Last Viceroy; **3 June Plan**; first GG of free India |
| **C. Rajagopalachari** | First & last Indian Governor-General |

### The Revolt of 1857
- Immediate cause: **Enfield rifle** greased cartridges. **Mangal Pandey** (34th Bengal Native Infantry) at **Barrackpore, 29 Mar 1857**. Revolt began at **Meerut, 10 May 1857**; rebels proclaimed **Bahadur Shah Zafar** emperor at Delhi.

| Centre | Leader | British commander who suppressed |
|---|---|---|
| Delhi | Bahadur Shah II; General **Bakht Khan** | Nicholson, Hodson |
| Kanpur | **Nana Saheb**, **Tantia Tope** | Colin Campbell |
| Lucknow | **Begum Hazrat Mahal** | Colin Campbell |
| Jhansi | **Rani Lakshmibai** (died at Gwalior, June 1858) | Hugh Rose |
| Jagdishpur (Bihar) | **Kunwar Singh** | William Taylor, Vincent Eyre |
| Faizabad | Maulvi Ahmadullah | — |
| Bareilly | Khan Bahadur Khan | — |
| Assam | **Maniram Dewan** (hanged 1858) | — |

- Result: **Government of India Act 1858** — Company rule ended; Crown rule; Secretary of State for India; **Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1 Nov 1858, Allahabad)**.
- V.D. Savarkar called it the "**First War of Indian Independence**" (1909).

lessons.title: National Movement: INC Sessions, Gandhian Era & Road to Independence
lessons.body:
### Indian National Congress — sessions to know

| Year | Place | President | Why remembered |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1885** | **Bombay** | **W.C. Bonnerjee** | Founding (28 Dec, 72 delegates), **A.O. Hume** |
| 1886 | Calcutta | Dadabhai Naoroji | |
| 1887 | Madras | **Badruddin Tyabji** | First Muslim president |
| 1888 | Allahabad | George Yule | First English president |
| 1896 | Calcutta | R.M. Sayani | **Vande Mataram** first sung (by Tagore) |
| 1905 | Banaras | G.K. Gokhale | Swadeshi endorsed |
| 1906 | Calcutta | Dadabhai Naoroji | **"Swaraj"** declared the goal |
| **1907** | **Surat** | Rash Behari Ghosh | **Split** — Moderates vs Extremists |
| **1911** | Calcutta | B.N. Dhar | **Jana Gana Mana** first sung (27 Dec) |
| **1916** | **Lucknow** | A.C. Majumdar | **Lucknow Pact** (INC–League); Moderates & Extremists reunite |
| 1917 | Calcutta | **Annie Besant** | First woman president |
| 1920 | Calcutta (special) / Nagpur | Lala Lajpat Rai / C. Vijayaraghavachariar | Non-Cooperation adopted / ratified |
| **1924** | **Belgaum** | **Mahatma Gandhi** | Only session Gandhi presided |
| 1925 | Kanpur | **Sarojini Naidu** | First Indian woman president |
| **1929** | **Lahore** | **Jawaharlal Nehru** | **Purna Swaraj**; 26 Jan 1930 celebrated as Independence Day |
| 1931 | Karachi | Vallabhbhai Patel | Resolution on **Fundamental Rights** & economic policy; endorsed Gandhi–Irwin Pact |
| 1938 | Haripura | **Subhas Chandra Bose** | National Planning Committee |
| 1939 | Tripuri | S.C. Bose (resigned) → Rajendra Prasad | Bose beat Pattabhi Sitaramayya |
| 1940 | Ramgarh | Maulana Azad | Remained president through 1940–46 (Quit India years) |
| 1946 | Meerut | **J.B. Kripalani** | President at Independence |

### Freedom struggle timeline
| Year | Event |
|---|---|
| 1905 | **Partition of Bengal** (effective 16 Oct) → **Swadeshi & Boycott**; Tagore's Raksha Bandhan, *Amar Sonar Bangla* |
| 1906 | **Muslim League** founded at **Dhaka** (Aga Khan, Nawab Salimullah) |
| 1913 | **Ghadar Party**, San Francisco (Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna) |
| 1916 | **Home Rule Leagues** — Tilak (April, Belgaum) & Annie Besant (Sept, Madras) |
| 1917 | **Champaran** (indigo; Raj Kumar Shukla) — Gandhi's first satyagraha in India |
| 1918 | **Ahmedabad mill strike** (first hunger strike) & **Kheda** (with Patel) |
| 1919 | **Rowlatt Act** satyagraha; **Jallianwala Bagh, 13 Apr** (Gen. Dyer); Tagore returned knighthood |
| 1919–22 | **Khilafat** (Ali brothers) & **Non-Cooperation** — withdrawn after **Chauri Chaura (5 Feb 1922)** |
| 1925 | **Kakori** train action (Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan) |
| 1927–28 | **Simon Commission** (no Indian member) — "Simon Go Back"; Lala Lajpat Rai fatally injured (1928); Nehru Report (Motilal Nehru) |
| 1929 | Bhagat Singh & B.K. Dutt bomb the Central Legislative Assembly (8 Apr) |
| 1930 | **Dandi March 12 Mar–6 Apr** (Sabarmati → Dandi, 78 followers, ~385 km) → **Civil Disobedience**; Chittagong armoury raid (Surya Sen); First Round Table Conference |
| 1931 | **Gandhi–Irwin Pact (5 Mar)**; Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru hanged (**23 Mar**); **Gandhi attends 2nd RTC** (only one he attended) |
| 1932 | **Communal Award** (Ramsay MacDonald) → Gandhi's fast → **Poona Pact (24 Sept) with Ambedkar** — reserved seats instead of separate electorates for depressed classes |
| 1935 | Government of India Act — provincial autonomy, federal court |
| 1940 | **Lahore Resolution** (Pakistan demand); **August Offer**; **Individual Satyagraha** — first satyagrahi **Vinoba Bhave**, second Nehru |
| 1942 | **Cripps Mission** ("post-dated cheque"); **Quit India, 8 Aug**, Gowalia Tank, Bombay — "**Do or Die**"; Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag |
| 1943 | Subhas Bose takes over **INA** (founded by Mohan Singh/Rash Behari Bose); **Azad Hind Govt, 21 Oct 1943, Singapore** — "Delhi Chalo", "Give me blood…" |
| 1945–46 | **INA trials at Red Fort** (Shah Nawaz, Sehgal, Dhillon; defended by Bhulabhai Desai); **RIN mutiny** (Bombay, Feb 1946); **Cabinet Mission** (Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps, A.V. Alexander) |
| 1946 | Direct Action Day (16 Aug); Interim Government (2 Sept, Nehru); Constituent Assembly meets (9 Dec) |
| 1947 | Attlee's statement (20 Feb); **Mountbatten Plan (3 June)**; Indian Independence Act; **Radcliffe Line**; Independence 15 Aug |

### Gandhi at a glance
- Born **2 Oct 1869, Porbandar**; South Africa 1893–1914 (Pietermaritzburg train incident, Natal Indian Congress 1894, Phoenix Settlement, Tolstoy Farm, *Indian Opinion*); returned **9 Jan 1915** (Pravasi Bharatiya Divas). Political guru **Gokhale**.
- Ashrams: Kochrab (1915) → **Sabarmati** (1917) → Sevagram/Wardha (1936).
- Papers: *Indian Opinion*, *Young India*, *Navajivan*, *Harijan*. Books: *Hind Swaraj* (1909), *My Experiments with Truth* (Gujarati *Satya na Prayogo*).
- "Father of the Nation" first used by **Subhas Bose** (radio, 1944); "half-naked fakir" — Churchill. Assassinated **30 Jan 1948** (Martyrs' Day).

### Slogans
| Slogan | Given by |
|---|---|
| "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it" | **Tilak** |
| "Do or Die" | Gandhi (Quit India) |
| "Inquilab Zindabad" | **Maulana Hasrat Mohani** (popularised by Bhagat Singh) |
| "Delhi Chalo", "Tum mujhe khoon do…" | Subhas Chandra Bose |
| "Jai Hind" | Popularised by INA/Bose (coined by Abid Hasan) |
| "Vande Mataram" | Bankim Chandra (*Anandamath*, 1882) |
| "Saare Jahan Se Achha" | Muhammad Iqbal |
| "Jai Jawan Jai Kisan" | Lal Bahadur Shastri (1965) |

lessons.title: Reformers, Personalities, Books & Newspapers
lessons.body:
### Socio-religious reformers & organisations

| Reformer | Organisation / work | Remember |
|---|---|---|
| **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** | Atmiya Sabha (1815), **Brahmo Samaj (1828)**; *Sambad Kaumudi* | "Father of the Indian Renaissance"; campaign behind **Sati abolition (1829)** |
| Debendranath Tagore | Tattvabodhini Sabha (1839) | Revived Brahmo Samaj |
| Keshab Chandra Sen | Brahmo Samaj of India (1866) | Native Marriage Act 1872 |
| Henry Vivian Derozio | **Young Bengal** movement | Hindu College teacher |
| **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** | Widow remarriage — **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act 1856** | *Barna Parichay* |
| Atmaram Pandurang / **M.G. Ranade** | **Prarthana Samaj (1867)**, Bombay | |
| **Swami Dayananda Saraswati** | **Arya Samaj (1875, Bombay)** | *Satyarth Prakash*; "Back to the Vedas"; Shuddhi |
| **Swami Vivekananda** | **Ramakrishna Mission (1897)**, Belur | Chicago Parliament of Religions (1893); birthday 12 Jan = National Youth Day |
| **Jyotiba Phule** | **Satyashodhak Samaj (1873)** | *Gulamgiri*; with **Savitribai Phule** first girls' school, Pune (1848) |
| **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** | Aligarh Movement; Scientific Society (1864); MAO College (1875 → AMU 1920) | *Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq* |
| Blavatsky & Olcott; **Annie Besant** | **Theosophical Society** (New York 1875; Adyar, Madras); Central Hindu College, Banaras (1898) | |
| **Sree Narayana Guru** | **SNDP Yogam (1903)**, Kerala | "One caste, one religion, one God for man" |
| **E.V. Ramasamy 'Periyar'** | **Self-Respect Movement (1925)** | Vaikom Satyagraha (1924–25) |
| **Dr B.R. Ambedkar** | Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924); **Mahad Satyagraha (1927)**; *Mooknayak*; Independent Labour Party (1936) | *Annihilation of Caste* |
| Pandita Ramabai | Arya Mahila Samaj, Sharada Sadan | |
| D.K. Karve | Women's university, Pune (1916) → SNDT | |
| Behramji Malabari | **Age of Consent Act (1891)** | |
| — | **Sarda Act 1929** (Child Marriage Restraint) | |

### Books & authors (freedom era)

| Book | Author |
|---|---|
| *Anandamath* (1882) — contains *Vande Mataram* | **Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay** |
| *Neel Darpan* (1860, indigo) | **Dinabandhu Mitra** |
| *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India* — "Drain Theory" | **Dadabhai Naoroji** |
| *Economic History of India* | R.C. Dutt |
| *Gita Rahasya* (written in Mandalay jail); *The Arctic Home in the Vedas* | **B.G. Tilak** |
| *Hind Swaraj*; *My Experiments with Truth* | **M.K. Gandhi** |
| *The Discovery of India* (Ahmednagar Fort jail); *Glimpses of World History*; *An Autobiography* | **Jawaharlal Nehru** |
| *India Wins Freedom* | **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** |
| *The Indian Struggle* | **Subhas Chandra Bose** |
| *Why I Am an Atheist* | **Bhagat Singh** |
| *The Indian War of Independence, 1857* | **V.D. Savarkar** |
| *Unhappy India* (reply to Katherine Mayo's *Mother India*) | **Lala Lajpat Rai** |
| *Annihilation of Caste*; *Pakistan or the Partition of India* | **B.R. Ambedkar** |
| *Gulamgiri* | Jyotiba Phule |
| *Satyarth Prakash* | Dayananda Saraswati |
| *Gitanjali* (Nobel 1913) | Rabindranath Tagore |
| *India Divided* | Rajendra Prasad |
| *Freedom at Midnight* | Larry Collins & Dominique Lapierre |

### Newspapers & journals
| Paper | Founder / editor |
|---|---|
| *Bengal Gazette* (1780) — first Indian newspaper | James Augustus **Hicky** |
| *Kesari* (Marathi), *Mahratta* (English) | **Tilak** |
| *Young India*, *Navajivan*, *Harijan*, *Indian Opinion* | **Gandhi** |
| *Al-Hilal*, *Al-Balagh* | **Maulana Azad** |
| *Comrade*, *Hamdard* | Maulana Mohammad Ali |

### Key personalities — titles
| Title | Person |
|---|---|
| Grand Old Man of India | Dadabhai Naoroji (first Indian in British Parliament, 1892) |
| Lokmanya | B.G. Tilak |

lessons.title: History of North-East India: Ahoms, Anglo-Burmese Wars & Treaty of Yandabo
lessons.body:
### Ancient & medieval kingdoms of the North-East

| Kingdom | Key facts |
|---|---|
| **Kamarupa** | Varman dynasty — **Bhaskaravarman** (7th c.), contemporary & ally of Harsha; **Hiuen Tsang** visited; later Mlechchha & Pala dynasties |
| **Ahom** (1228–1826) | Founded by **Sukaphaa** (Chaolung Sukapha), a Tai prince from **Mong Mao** (Yunnan–Myanmar borderland), who entered Assam across the **Patkai** hills in **1228**; ruled ~600 years |
| Koch | **Nara Narayan** and his general-brother **Chilarai** (16th c.) |
| Kachari (Dimasa) | Capitals Dimapur → Maibang → Khaspur |
| Manipur (Kangleipak) | Meitei kings; Kangla Fort; **Anglo-Manipur War 1891** — **Bir Tikendrajit** hanged (13 Aug, Patriots' Day); **Battle of Khongjom** (23 Apr 1891, Paona Brajabashi) |
| Tripura | **Manikya dynasty**; chronicle **Rajmala** |

### The Ahoms — what gets asked
| Topic | Fact |
|---|---|
| Capitals | **Charaideo** (first; royal burial mounds), Garhgaon, **Rangpur (Sivasagar)** |
| Administration | **Paik system** — every adult male owed labour/military service; ministers Borgohain, Burhagohain, Borpatrogohain; **Borphukan** (viceroy of Lower Assam), Borbarua |
| Chronicles | **Buranjis** — written histories (Tai-Ahom, later Assamese) |
| **Battle of Saraighat (1671)** | Ahom general **Lachit Borphukan** defeated the **Mughal** army of **Raja Ram Singh I** (sent by Aurangzeb) on the **Brahmaputra near Guwahati** — a naval battle; **Lachit Divas 24 Nov**; NDA's best-cadet gold medal is named after him |
| Monuments | **Rang Ghar** (royal pavilion/amphitheatre, Pramatta Singha), **Talatal Ghar**, **Kareng Ghar**; **Charaideo Moidams** — UNESCO World Heritage Site (**2024**), first cultural WHS in the North-East |
| Great kings | Suhungmung (Dihingia Raja, adopted Hindu title "Swarganarayan"), Pratap Singha, **Gadadhar Singha**, **Rudra Singha** (height of power) |
| Decline | **Moamoria rebellion** (1769 onwards); court intrigues; **Burmese invasions 1817, 1819, 1821** ("Manor Upadrav") |
| Days | **Sukapha Divas / Asom Divas — 2 December** |

### Anglo-Burmese Wars and the Treaty of Yandabo

| War | Years | Governor-General | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| **First** | **1824–26** | **Lord Amherst** | **Treaty of Yandabo, 24 Feb 1826** |
| Second | 1852 | Lord Dalhousie | Lower Burma (Pegu) annexed |
| Third | 1885 | Lord Dufferin | Upper Burma annexed (king Thibaw exiled); Burma annexed 1 Jan 1886 |

**Treaty of Yandabo (1826)** — signed at Yandabo village on the Irrawaddy near Ava:
- Burma **renounced claims over Assam, Manipur, Cachar and Jaintia**;
- **ceded Arakan and Tenasserim** to the British;
- paid a war indemnity of **£1 million** (in instalments);
- accepted a British Resident at Ava and a commercial treaty.
- Consequence: British entry into the North-East; **Assam** came under Company control (David Scott as Agent to the GG, North-East Frontier). Upper Assam was briefly restored to **Purandar Singha** (1833) and annexed in **1838**; **Cachar** annexed 1832, **Jaintia** 1835.

### Colonial-era NE — other must-knows
| Item | Fact |
|---|---|
| Tea | **Robert Bruce** found wild tea in Assam (1823) with Singpho chief Bisa Gam; **Assam Company (1839)** |
| Inner Line | **Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, 1873** |
| Anglo-Bhutan (Duar) War | 1864–65 → **Treaty of Sinchula** (Duars ceded) |
| Lushai expedition | 1871–72 |
| 1857 in Assam | **Maniram Dewan** (Maniram Dutta Barua) & Piyali Barua hanged (1858) |
| Early resistance | Gomdhar Konwar (1828), Anglo-Khasi resistance of U Tirot Sing (1829–33) — *see Meghalaya module for state-specific history* |
| Naga freedom fighter | **Rani Gaidinliu** — Heraka movement with Haipou Jadonang; arrested 1932; title "Rani" by Nehru |
| Quit India in Assam | **Kanaklata Barua** (17, shot at **Gohpur** police station, 20 Sept 1942, carrying the Tricolour); **Kushal Konwar** (hanged 1943); Bhogeswari Phukanani |
| Leaders | **Gopinath Bordoloi** — first CM of Assam, resisted inclusion of Assam in Group C of the Cabinet Mission plan; **Bharat Ratna 1999** |
| Assam reformer-writer | Chandraprabha Saikiani (women's rights), Lakshminath Bezbaroa (*O Mur Apunar Desh*) |

examples.q: Type: Site → feature (IVC). 'The dockyard of the Harappan civilisation was found at (a) Kalibangan (b) Lothal (c) Harappa (d) Ropar'
examples.solution:
Step 1: A dockyard needs sea access — only a coastal Gujarat site fits.
Step 2: Lothal (Gujarat, on the Bhogava near the Gulf of Khambhat) is the port-town; Kalibangan (Rajasthan) = ploughed field; Harappa = granaries; Ropar = dog burial.
Answer: (b) Lothal
examples.shortcut: Geography decides: coast → Lothal/Dholavira; desert river → Kalibangan; Sindh → Mohenjo-daro/Chanhudaro.

examples.q: Type: Book → author. 'Who wrote The Indian Struggle?'
examples.solution:
Step 1: Recall the author clusters — Nehru (Discovery of India, Glimpses), Azad (India Wins Freedom), Bose (The Indian Struggle), Tilak (Gita Rahasya), Naoroji (Poverty and Un-British Rule).
Step 2: 'The Indian Struggle' (1920–42) = Subhas Chandra Bose.
Answer: Subhas Chandra Bose
examples.shortcut: Link each book to the author's life: Azad wrote about winning freedom; Bose about the struggle; Nehru discovered India in jail.

examples.q: Type: INC session → president/event. 'At which session was the Purna Swaraj resolution passed?'
examples.solution:
Step 1: Purna Swaraj = December 1929, which led to 26 January 1930 being observed as Independence Day.
Step 2: The 1929 session was at Lahore on the Ravi, presided by Jawaharlal Nehru.
Answer: Lahore, 1929 (Nehru)
examples.shortcut: Anchor sessions: 1885 Bombay (birth), 1907 Surat (split), 1916 Lucknow (pact), 1924 Belgaum (Gandhi), 1929 Lahore (Purna Swaraj), 1931 Karachi (FRs), 1938 Haripura (Bose).

examples.q: Type: Chronology. 'Arrange: Plassey, Buxar, Third Panipat, Wandiwash.'
examples.solution:
Step 1: Plassey 1757.
Step 2: Wandiwash 1760 (French finished).
Step 3: Third Panipat 1761 (Marathas weakened).
Step 4: Buxar 1764 (Mughal-Nawab alliance crushed) → Allahabad 1765.
Answer: Plassey – Wandiwash – Panipat III – Buxar
examples.shortcut: 57-60-61-64-65: 'Plassey, then the French, then the Marathas, then Buxar and Diwani'.

examples.q: Type: North-East history. 'The Treaty of Yandabo was signed between the British and (a) Ahoms (b) Burmese (c) Manipuris (d) Bhutanese'
examples.solution:
Step 1: Yandabo is a village on the Irrawaddy in Burma.
Step 2: It ended the First Anglo-Burmese War (1824–26) under Lord Amherst on 24 Feb 1826; Burma gave up Assam, Manipur, Cachar and Jaintia and ceded Arakan & Tenasserim.
Answer: (b) Burmese
examples.shortcut: Treaty with Bhutan = Sinchula (1865); with Burma = Yandabo (1826); with Sikhs = Amritsar (1809), Lahore (1846).

traps: Mohenjo-daro vs Harappa: the Great Bath, Dancing Girl and Priest-King are all from MOHENJO-DARO; Harappa is famous for granaries and being the first excavated. Chanhudaro is the city without a citadel.
Tarain: the FIRST battle (1191) was won by Prithviraj Chauhan; the SECOND (1192) by Muhammad Ghori. Panipat: 1526 Babur–Ibrahim Lodi; 1556 Akbar (Bairam Khan)–Hemu; 1761 Abdali–Marathas.

First Governor-General of Bengal = Warren Hastings (1773); first Governor-General of India = William Bentinck (1833); first Viceroy = Canning (1858); first GG of free India = Mountbatten; first & last Indian GG = C. Rajagopalachari.

First woman INC president = Annie Besant (1917, Calcutta); first INDIAN woman president = Sarojini Naidu (1925, Kanpur). Vande Mataram first sung at INC in 1896; Jana Gana Mana in 1911 — both in Calcutta.
Saraighat (1671) was Ahoms vs MUGHALS (not Burmese). The Burmese invaded Assam in 1817–21, and the British expelled them in the First Anglo-Burmese War ending with Yandabo (1826).

Gandhi attended only the SECOND Round Table Conference (1931), presided over only ONE INC session (Belgaum 1924), and his first satyagraha in India was Champaran (1917) — not Kheda or Ahmedabad (1918).

practice.q: The Great Bath of the Indus Valley Civilisation was discovered at
practice.explanation:
The Great Bath is at Mohenjo-daro (Sindh), along with the Great Granary, Dancing Girl and Priest-King.
Hook: 'Mohenjo-daro — the Mound of the Dead had the biggest bath.'

practice.q: Evidence of a ploughed field and fire altars of the Harappan period has been found at
practice.explanation:
Kalibangan (Rajasthan, on the Ghaggar) shows a ploughed field and fire altars; Lothal = dockyard; Chanhudaro = bead-making.
Hook: 'Kali-bangan — black bangles and a ploughed field.'

practice.q: The national motto 'Satyameva Jayate' is taken from the
practice.explanation:
'Satyameva Jayate' (Truth alone triumphs) is from the Mundaka Upanishad; it appears below the Sarnath Lion Capital emblem.
Hook: 'Mundaka — Motto.'

practice.q: Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon at
practice.explanation:
Born Lumbini → enlightened Bodh Gaya → first sermon Sarnath (Dharmachakra Pravartana) → died Kushinagar.
Hook: 'L-B-S-K: Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar.'

practice.q: The Fourth Buddhist Council, which led to the division into Hinayana and Mahayana, was held under the patronage of
practice.explanation:
4th Council in Kashmir under Kanishka (chair Vasumitra). 1st Ajatashatru, 2nd Kalashoka, 3rd Ashoka.
Hook: 'A-K-A-K: Ajatashatru, Kalashoka, Ashoka, Kanishka.'

practice.q: 'Indica', an account of Mauryan India, was written by
practice.explanation:
Megasthenes, envoy of Seleucus Nicator at Chandragupta Maurya's court, wrote Indica. Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind; Hiuen Tsang wrote Si-yu-ki.
Hook: 'Mega-sthenes for the mega Mauryan empire.'

practice.q: The Brahmi script of Ashoka's inscriptions was first deciphered in 1837 by
practice.explanation:
James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi (1837). William Jones founded the Asiatic Society (1784); Cunningham was the first ASI Director-General; Marshall led the Indus excavations.
Hook: 'Prinsep printed Ashoka's words.'

practice.q: The Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription), composed by Harisena, describes the conquests of
practice.explanation:
Harisena, court poet of Samudragupta, composed the Prayag Prashasti on an Ashokan pillar at Allahabad.
Hook: 'Harisena sang Samudragupta — the Napoleon of India.'

practice.q: The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of
practice.explanation:
Fa-Hien (Faxian) came during Chandragupta II Vikramaditya (c. 399–411 CE); Hiuen Tsang came during Harsha.
Hook: 'Fa-Hien — Gupta; Hiuen Tsang — Harsha.'

practice.q: Who among the following wrote 'Harshacharita'?
practice.explanation:
Banabhatta, Harsha's court poet, wrote Harshacharita and Kadambari. Kalhana wrote Rajatarangini (Kashmir).
Hook: 'Bana praised Harsha.'

practice.q: The monolithic Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by the
practice.explanation:
Built under Rashtrakuta king Krishna I (8th century), carved from a single rock. Pallavas built Mahabalipuram; Cholas the Brihadeeswara temple.
Hook: 'Rashtrakuta — Rock-cut Kailasa.'

practice.q: The Second Battle of Tarain (1192) was fought between
practice.explanation:
1191: Prithviraj won; 1192: Ghori won, laying the foundation of Turkish rule. Ghori beat Jaichand at Chandawar (1194).
Hook: 'Round 1 Prithviraj, Round 2 Ghori.'

practice.q: Which Sultan of Delhi introduced token currency?
practice.explanation:
Muhammad bin Tughlaq issued bronze/copper token coins and also shifted the capital to Daulatabad (1327).
Hook: 'Tughlaq's two experiments — tokens and transfer.'

practice.q: The first and only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate was
practice.explanation:
Razia Sultan (1236–40), daughter of Iltutmish. Nur Jahan was a Mughal empress-consort; Chand Bibi defended Ahmednagar.
Hook: 'Razia reigned; others ruled from behind.'

practice.q: Market control reforms, branding of horses (dagh) and a descriptive roll of soldiers (chehra) are associated with
practice.explanation:
Alauddin Khalji fixed prices and maintained a large standing army to repel the Mongols.
Hook: 'Alauddin's Lamp controlled the market.'

practice.q: The Vijayanagara empire was founded in 1336 by
practice.explanation:
Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty founded it on the Tungabhadra. Bahman Shah founded the Bahmani kingdom (1347).
Hook: '1336 — two brothers, one capital: Hampi.'

practice.q: The Battle of Talikota, which led to the decline of Vijayanagara, was fought in
practice.explanation:
Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi), 1565 — Deccan sultanates defeated Vijayanagara. 1526 = Panipat I, 1556 = Panipat II, 1576 = Haldighati.
Hook: 'Talikota 65 — Hampi's end.'

practice.q: Babur defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar in the Battle of
practice.explanation:
Khanwa 1527 — Rana Sanga. Panipat 1526 — Ibrahim Lodi; Chanderi 1528 — Medini Rai; Ghaghra 1529 — Afghans.
Hook: 'Babur's four wins, one per year: P-K-C-G.'

practice.q: The silver coin 'rupiya' was introduced by
practice.explanation:
Sher Shah Suri (1540–45) issued the silver rupiya and developed the Grand Trunk Road and sarais.
Hook: 'Sher Shah — the rupee and the road.'

practice.q: 'Ain-i-Akbari' was written by
practice.explanation:
Abul Fazl wrote Akbarnama, of which Ain-i-Akbari is the third volume. Gulbadan Begum wrote Humayun-nama.
Hook: 'Abul Fazl — Akbar's biographer.'

practice.q: The Khalsa was founded in 1699 at Anandpur Sahib by
practice.explanation:
Guru Gobind Singh, the 10th Guru, founded the Khalsa and declared the Granth Sahib the eternal Guru.
Hook: 'Tenth Guru, final form — Khalsa.'

practice.q: Arrange the following battles in chronological order: 1. Plassey 2. Buxar 3. Third Battle of Panipat 4. Wandiwash
practice.explanation:
Plassey 1757 → Wandiwash 1760 → Panipat III 1761 → Buxar 1764.
Hook: '57-60-61-64.'

practice.q: The 'Doctrine of Lapse' was applied by
practice.explanation:
Dalhousie (1848–56) annexed Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur etc. under the Doctrine of Lapse. Wellesley = Subsidiary Alliance; Cornwallis = Permanent Settlement.
Hook: 'Dalhousie — Doctrine.'

practice.q: The Permanent Settlement of land revenue in Bengal (1793) was introduced by
practice.explanation:
Cornwallis fixed revenue permanently with zamindars in 1793.
Hook: 'Cornwallis — permanently fixed corn-fields.'

practice.q: The Revolt of 1857 formally began at Meerut on
practice.explanation:
Sepoys rose at Meerut on 10 May 1857 and marched to Delhi. 29 March 1857 = Mangal Pandey at Barrackpore; 1 Nov 1858 = Queen's Proclamation.
Hook: 'Mangal in March, Meerut in May.'

practice.q: Who led the Revolt of 1857 at Lucknow?
practice.explanation:
Begum Hazrat Mahal (Awadh/Lucknow); Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi); Kunwar Singh (Jagdishpur, Bihar); Nana Saheb (Kanpur).
Hook: 'Lucknow's Begum, Jhansi's Rani.'

practice.q: Who was the first President of the Indian National Congress?
practice.explanation:
W.C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session, Bombay, 28 Dec 1885; A.O. Hume was the founder-organiser.
Hook: 'Bonnerjee in Bombay.'

practice.q: The 'Purna Swaraj' resolution was adopted at which session of the Congress?
practice.explanation:
Lahore 1929 under Nehru; 26 Jan 1930 celebrated as Purna Swaraj Day — later the date of Republic Day.
Hook: 'Lahore on the Ravi, 1929 — complete freedom.'

practice.q: The only session of the Indian National Congress presided over by Mahatma Gandhi was held at
practice.explanation:
Belgaum 1924. Kanpur 1925 — Sarojini Naidu; Lahore 1929 — Nehru; Haripura 1938 — Subhas Bose.
Hook: 'Gandhi's only gavel — Belgaum.'

practice.q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn in 1922 following the violent incident at
practice.explanation:
Police station set on fire at Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur), 5 Feb 1922; Gandhi called off NCM.
Hook: 'Chauri Chaura — the stop sign.'

practice.q: The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed between
options: Jawaharlal Nehru and Liaquat Ali Khan
Mahatma Gandhi and Dr B.R. Ambedkar
practice.explanation:
After the Communal Award, Gandhi fasted at Yerawada; the Poona Pact gave reserved seats in joint electorates to depressed classes. Gandhi–Irwin Pact was 1931.
Hook: 'Poona — Gandhi & Ambedkar; Delhi — Gandhi & Irwin.'

practice.q: Who was chosen by Gandhi as the first individual satyagrahi in 1940?
practice.explanation:
Individual Satyagraha (Oct 1940): Vinoba Bhave first, Nehru second.
Hook: 'V before N — Vinoba, then Nehru.'

practice.q: 'Satyashodhak Samaj' was founded by
practice.explanation:
Jyotiba Phule founded Satyashodhak Samaj (1873) and wrote Gulamgiri. Narayana Guru — SNDP; Periyar — Self-Respect Movement; Dayananda — Arya Samaj.
Hook: 'Satya-shodhak — truth-seeker Phule.'

practice.q: Which of the following pairs of book and author is NOT correctly matched?
options: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India – Dadabhai Naoroji
India Wins Freedom – Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
The Indian Struggle – Subhas Chandra Bose
practice.explanation:
Anandamath (1882), which contains 'Vande Mataram', is by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
Hook: 'Bankim wrote the song; Tagore sang it (1896).'

practice.q: The Ahom kingdom in Assam was founded in 1228 by
practice.explanation:
Sukaphaa, a Tai prince from Mong Mao, crossed the Patkai hills in 1228; 2 December is observed as Sukapha Divas/Asom Divas.
Hook: '1228 — Sukaphaa starts 600 years.'

practice.q: In the Battle of Saraighat (1671), the Ahom forces under Lachit Borphukan defeated the
practice.explanation:
Lachit defeated the Mughal army of Raja Ram Singh I (sent by Aurangzeb) in a naval battle on the Brahmaputra near Guwahati. Lachit Divas: 24 November.
Hook: 'Saraighat saved Assam from Aurangzeb.'

practice.q: The Treaty of Yandabo (1826) brought to an end the
practice.explanation:
The First Anglo-Burmese War (1824–26, Lord Amherst) ended with the Treaty of Yandabo, 24 Feb 1826. Anglo-Bhutan War ended with the Treaty of Sinchula (1865).
Hook: 'Yandabo = Year One of British Assam.'

practice.q: Which one of the following was NOT a provision of the Treaty of Yandabo?
options: Burma ceded Arakan and Tenasserim to the British
Burma renounced its claims over Assam, Manipur, Cachar and Jaintia
Burma agreed to pay a war indemnity of one million pounds
Burma ceded Upper Burma and its king was exiled
practice.explanation:
Upper Burma was annexed only after the Third Anglo-Burmese War (1885), when King Thibaw was exiled. Yandabo (1826) covered the other three terms.
Hook: 'Yandabo took the edges; 1885 took the core.'

practice.q: Kanaklata Barua, a 17-year-old martyr of Assam, was shot while leading a procession to hoist the Tricolour at Gohpur police station during the
practice.explanation:
Kanaklata Barua was killed on 20 September 1942 during the Quit India Movement at Gohpur (then Darrang district, now Biswanath district).
Hook: '1942, age 17, flag at Gohpur.'

practice.q: Who was the Governor-General of India when the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi (announced 1911)?
practice.explanation:
Announced at the Delhi Durbar (Dec 1911) under Lord Hardinge II, along with annulment of the Bengal partition. Curzon partitioned Bengal (1905).
Hook: 'Curzon cut Bengal; Hardinge healed it and moved to Delhi.'
